They will ask you to provide documentation (e.g. employment separation notice, writing no longer employed on your last paycheck, etc). 

Next, you will get a notice with the date of your hearing. Make sure to keep this letter. It will have a lot of information regarding the appeals process. On the day of your hearing, call in when prompted. When you are connected to the judge, state your name and state that you want to appeal the unemployment decision. 

They will lead you through the hearing. They will ask questions and you will have the opportunity to ask questions as well. The judge may ask you to provide additional documentation (e.g. IDs, addresses, etc). It’s very important to provide them with accurate information. They will inform you of their decision in 3-4 weeks. 

Best of luck!

Provide your ex with a copy of your SF-50 "Letter of Eligibility" for the FEHB. They have to be covered under your policy for 18 months after divorce.
Fill out the OPM mid-year divorce form (form SF3107) and have your ex sign it, too. Apparently this form authorizes the Office of Personnel Management to split your retirement benefits with your ex. Choose to either keep your ex as your beneficiary (not recommended) or change your beneficiary to a new person. Obviously, you'll need a new person if you're remarried. You can do this by submitting a new FEHB enrollment form.
That's pretty much it from what I remember. Hopefully that helps.
